title: TradeTrap: Are LLM-based Trading Agents Truly Reliable and Faithful?

task.value: Stress-testing the reliability and robustness of LLM-based autonomous trading agents (Adaptive and Procedural) under controlled system-level adversarial perturbations.
task.quote: We propose TradeTrap, a unified evaluation framework for systematically stress-testing both Adaptive and Procedural autonomous trading agents.

architecture.value: Unified evaluation agent with external data interfaces (market data, social media, fundamentals), prompt-driven reasoning, memory/state, and execution via brokerage APIs; Adaptive (tool-calling, e.g. AI-Trader) and Procedural (fixed pipeline, e.g. NoFX/ValueCell) variants; attack modules inject perturbations.
architecture.quote: although existing trading agents differ in internal control flow, they all share a common functional structure composed of external data interfaces, prompt-driven reasoning, internal memory/state, and execution modules.

data.value: Historical U.S. equity market data; universe of approximately 100 NASDAQ-100 stocks, replayed chronologically; news and social-media (X, Reddit) feeds.
data.quote: The trading universe consists of approximately 100 stocks from the NASDAQ-100 index. Market data are replayed in chronological order to simulate live trading conditions.

window.value: Backtest from October 1 to October 31 (year not specified in text); no train/validation split described.
window.quote: The evaluation period spans from October 1 to October 31.

baselines.value: Clean (unattacked) runs of each agent type, and the QQQ index benchmark.
baselines.quote: All other components—including market data, prompts, memory mechanisms, execution logic, and risk constraints—remain identical to the clean baseline setting.

headline_result.value: Under state tampering, the Procedural agent's total return fell from 0.91% to -61.02% over the October evaluation month, with max drawdown 91.97%; final NAV $1928.82 from $5000.
headline_result.quote: The clean baseline achieves a total return of 0.91% with 9.29% volatility and 1.59% maximum drawdown, whereas the tampered agent suffers a total loss of 61.02% with an annualized return of -100%.

costs.value: Transaction fees and slippage are not included; risk-free rate set to zero for Sharpe.
costs.quote: Transaction fees and slippage are not included in the current evaluation, so all reported results reflect pure strategy and execution effects.

release.quote: Our code is public at https://github.com/Yanlewen/TradeTrap.
